title: Regularity of Post-Period Mean Intervals under Nonunique Tangential Wasserstein Projection Plans
banked_reason: TERMINAL:BELOW-FLOOR — achieved tier incremental; required floor field; the finite exhaustive singular-arc certificate remains unproved and the paper-score ceiling is 5.3 below 7.4.
gap_reasons: The headline primitive necessary-and-sufficient certificate is under-delivered: its finite, auditable enumeration of bounded-degree Thom-encoded Puiseux arc families is inferred from two unproved lemmas without precise theorem-level citations covering the asserted effectiveness and completeness.

The singular-arc argument establishes generic semialgebraic witness existence at most, but does not construct or prove exhaustion of the finite incidence certificate advertised in the TL;DR and project justification.
The Gaussian result also applies a local expansion proved on the constrained mass domain to empirical primitives that can leave that domain when the base has a cell mass equal to its lower bound.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a finite endpoint atlas, exact-algebraic endpoint reduction, all-plan extension, four separating benchmark families, and a solver-robust whole-interval confidence construction. The field-level claim collapsed because qualitative semialgebraic arc selection did not prove the advertised finite exhaustive Thom/Puiseux incidence certificate; completing it requires a new quantitative substrate program, while the remaining Gaussian neighborhood repair is only local.
tldr: For fixed finite real-algebraic supports, exactly encoded rational or real-algebraic base masses, and positive population cell masses, the paper proves an exact active-face atlas and a terminating primitive necessary-and-sufficient certificate for the entire all-plan/all-weight TWP post-mean interval. The certificate separately decides width order, common-center Hadamard directional differentiability, derivative continuity and linearity, endpoint persistence, and Hausdorff order, including determinant-zero boundaries through smaller-support charts and singular closure-incidence arcs. Primitive-region projection covers the whole interval under arbitrary exact solver selection. Its certified contraction rate is \(n^{-\beta_H/2}\) when the certificate is run with lower mass bound \(\epsilon/2\), the same domain searched by the confidence region; locally constant targets are recovered exactly with probability tending to one, while a Hausdorff jump forbids uniform shrinkage. The four atomic benchmarks also show that transport-face interiors matter and that quadratic width does not imply a linear Gaussian regime.
gap: The founding TWP paper conditions uniqueness on selected optimal plans. KlattMunkZemel2022 and LiuBuneaNilesWeed2023 hold the LP matrix and objective fixed while perturbing its right-hand side; noisy-QP inference uses generic KKT restrictions, semialgebraic theory supplies high-level Hölder properties, and Gaussian regularized-LP inference assumes a unique population optimizer. None supplies a primitive iff boundary for the varying transport-face, plan-dependent Gram/QP, post-mean image or its all-selection inferential consequences.
fill: Derive and prove completeness of an incidence-based certificate, convert the face/chart atlas into independently checkable endpoint witnesses and useful conditioning diagnostics, and link each geometric regime to a valid whole-interval inference rule and an adaptation lower bound. Generic elimination and confidence projection are retained only as baselines.
